[untitled BTM module] The grouping is anchored on post-transcriptional and transcriptional control of gene expression in neural and developing tissues. Three sequence-specific RNA-binding proteins carry much of its identity: the neuronal ELAV-family protein ELAVL3 and the cytoplasmic polyadenylation element binding protein CPEB3 govern stability, localisation and translation of mRNAs in neurons, where CPEB3 acts on transcripts encoding glutamate receptor subunits and contributes to synaptic plasticity and memory, while YBX1 is a broadly acting mRNA packaging and translational regulator.

[untitled BTM module] The dominant theme here is transmembrane solute handling in polarized epithelia of liver and kidney, coupled to regulated vesicular secretion. Several members are plasma-membrane carriers that set how nutrients and ions cross epithelial barriers: GLUT2 moves glucose across hepatocyte and beta-cell membranes and underlies glucose sensing, the organic cation transporter SLC22A2 clears cationic drugs and metabolites in the proximal tubule, SLC6A13 imports betaine and GABA, and the copper-transporting ATPase ATP7B loads copper onto ceruloplasmin and excretes excess into bile, its loss causing Wnson disease.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on the braking and tuning of growth-factor signalling as it feeds into transcription, a control layer whose loss produces overgrowth, cancer and neurodevelopmental disease. Two GTPase-activating proteins, RASA2 for Ras and ACAP2 for an Arf-family GTPase, terminate signalling at the membrane, while MAP3K2 relays kinase input downstream and sorting nexins SNX13 and SNX14 govern endosomal trafficking and receptor fate.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on nuclear organisation and nucleocytoplasmic traffic: chromatin architecture, mRNA processing, ribosome biogenesis and export of cargo through the nuclear pore. CTCF and the cohesin subunit SMC1A together define chromatin loop boundaries and insulate promoters from inappropriate enhancers, which is how genome folding is translated into transcriptional output; ADNP and ATF1 act on transcription, the latter as a CREB-family factor responding to cAMP signalling.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on the fat cell as a lipid-storing endocrine organ. Leptin is the adipocyte-derived hormone that reports fat mass to hypothalamic circuits controlling appetite and energy expenditure, and its loss causes severe hyperphagic obesity.
